secondSection.title: Regular and irregular verbs
secondSection.description: According to the method of forming the past indefinite tense and the second participle, all English verbs are divided into regular and irregular.

content.text: Most English verbs are regular verbs, the formation of the past indefinite tense and participle II of which is carried out using the ending -ed:
If the stem ends in -e, then after adding -ed, only one letter -e is written:
If the verb stem ends in a consonant and -y, then y changes to -i:
In British English, if this final consonant is -l, it is doubled regardless of stress:

content.title: Irregular verbs
content.description: There is also a group of verbs in English for which the second and third forms are formed in a special way. These are called irregular English verbs.
content.listDescription: There are several main ways of forming irregular verb forms:
